subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Free Trade Zones
description: A fast breakdown of Free Trade Zones for builders.

hook.text: Goods sit in a warehouse inside a country but legally haven't entered it yet. That's a free trade zone.

buildup.text: Free trade zones (FTZs) are designated areas where goods can be stored, assembled, or processed duty-free.

discovery.text: Duties are paid only when goods enter the domestic market. If re-exported, no duty is owed at all.

twist.text: Companies use FTZs to delay duty payments, improve cash flow, and reduce costs on re-exported goods.

climax.text: Dubai's Jebel Ali Free Zone hosts 8,700+ companies and handles 30% of the region's trade volume.

punchline.text: Inside the border but outside the tariff. That's the trick.

quiz.question: When are duties paid in a free trade zone?
options: When goods arrive at the zone
Only when goods enter the domestic market
